reasons.rubric: Boolean freshness predicate with revocable employer credential, but employers rarely issue credentials, issuers are fragmented and landlords often want salary level.
reasons.validity: Landlords do ask for employment proof, but 'currently employed' is often insufficient without income, and the title's 'night-market stall helper' and 'phone plan' framing does not match the landlord moment.
reasons.coherence: Title (staff-only phone plan or viewing slot) mismatches the body (landlord rent discount), and the predicate omits income which the verifier usually needs.
reasons.novelty: Employment status for rental screening is a close variant of the known rental and loan cases with a different predicate.
reasons.retention_law: Private landlord has no known duty to retain the full certificate, though Taiwanese rules on this are unclear to me.
reasons.linkability: A fresh proof naming the employer with a 24-hour freshness window is low-risk, but repeated proofs against a small employer could link the holder.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Small employers have little incentive or infrastructure to sign and revoke credentials, which is a serious obstacle.
reasons.no_wallet: Landlords can fall back to paper certificates, so adoption would be voluntary and slow.

reasons.rubric: Uniqueness plus eligibility needs two credentials from fragmented issuers and is a low-frequency event, so it needs design work.
reasons.validity: Building votes are real, but telco subscriber uniqueness does not establish residency or one vote per unit, and condominium governance typically weights votes by ownership and wants signed records.
reasons.coherence: The telco issuer proves the wrong thing (one person per SIM, not one per unit), so predicate and issuer do not fit without a second credential.
reasons.novelty: Anonymous uniqueness for a local poll is a new moment, though the nullifier predicate resembles the known brokerage Sybil case.
reasons.provenance: The sealed-bid and subpoena-log borrowings are loosely analogical; the hidden-until-close ballot idea is a generic voting property the idea would carry without the source.
reasons.retention_law: The condominium rules may require signed or recorded votes, which could block anonymity, but I cannot confirm the specifics.
reasons.linkability: Poll-scoped nullifier avoids cross-poll linking, but small electorates mean the unit or phone could be inferred from the tally.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Telcos have no obvious reason to issue a uniqueness credential for building polls.
reasons.no_wallet: Elderly residents without a compatible wallet would be excluded, and committees can simply keep using paper or LINE.

reasons.rubric: The predicate is a count-and-threshold over bank data from one existing issuer, but it needs a new bank-defined statistic and a payee tie, so it is a design problem with medium frequency.
reasons.validity: Landlords do ask for bank statements, but many rental decisions rely on income and guarantors, and the claim depends on a payee identity the bank would have to attest.
reasons.coherence: Parts fit well: over-collection, a bank issuer, and a bounded aggregate.
reasons.novelty: Rental is a known moment, but a payment-history predicate from a bank is a new predicate and issuer on it.
reasons.provenance: The borrowings only restate that verifiers over-collect documents, which is already in the disclosed_today field, so they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: A private landlord has no known duty to retain statements, though I am not certain of tenancy rules.
reasons.linkability: The proof names the payee and period, which could link the tenant to a specific prior landlord, a modest concern.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Banks do not offer such statistics today and have little commercial incentive.
reasons.no_wallet: Private landlords can keep accepting screenshots, so the tenant gains nothing unless the landlord opts in.

reasons.rubric: Multi-condition aggregate over bank transactions with no standard attestation puts this at needs-design.
reasons.validity: Landlords want rent history and buffer, but 'a rent-like payee' is vague and a balance buffer is an odd proxy, and a single-account claim is easily gamed.
reasons.coherence: Predicate and issuer fit, but the vague payee and the single-account limitation weaken the claim.
reasons.novelty: Nearly a duplicate of the sibling idea b11-2 with an added balance condition, so little new beyond a rewording of the rental screening case.
reasons.provenance: The borrowings only restate over-collection of documents, which the idea does not depend on, so they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: A private landlord has no known duty to retain statements, though I am not certain.
reasons.linkability: Proof reveals thresholds and period only, so linkability is low.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: No Taiwanese bank offers this and the aggregate is complex to define and sign.
reasons.no_wallet: Landlords can keep requesting statement photos, which defeats adoption.

reasons.rubric: Multi-source match between a university credential and national identity across fragmented universities, and the operator must retain real-name data anyway.
reasons.validity: Student plans exist, but the described risk is stolen-identity fraud on SIM registration, and the idea itself admits that real-name rules still require retaining ID data.
reasons.coherence: Title is a student-plan discount while the predicate is an identity-binding match, and the predicate is not a privacy-minimising disclosure but an anti-fraud binding.
reasons.novelty: Student status is near the known scholarship and degree cases, but telecom as verifier and holder-binding as the predicate are new.
reasons.provenance: The copyable-identifier failure motivates holder binding and shapes the central design, though the blind-token borrowing is not visibly used.
reasons.retention_law: The idea concedes that SIM real-name rules require the operator to retain ID data, which removes most of the benefit.
reasons.linkability: Binding match with two credentials from different issuers risks linking via shared holder key unless carefully designed.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Universities issuing wallet enrolment credentials is plausible but fragmented across institutions.
reasons.no_wallet: Shop counter customers without the national wallet can fall back on existing ID checks.

reasons.rubric: Threshold predicate on two metrics but sourced from a non-cooperating platform via zkTLS, low frequency and fragile.
reasons.validity: Pop-up organisers vetting sellers is a real niche, but the public shop page already shows ratings, and the stated thresholds may not be what organisers decide on.
reasons.coherence: Fits as a design, but the idea concedes the public page already provides most of the signal.
reasons.novelty: A seller-trust moment is near the known marketplace seller verification case, but the verifier and predicate differ.
reasons.retention_law: No known duty for an organiser to retain dashboard screenshots, but I am not certain.
reasons.linkability: A zkTLS proof reveals the shop identity if used to verify ownership, so it is linkable to the public shop anyway.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Shopee has not agreed to attest and the idea relies on scraping its seller center, which its terms may forbid.
reasons.no_wallet: Organisers can simply look at the public page or ask for screenshots, and zkTLS needs tooling sellers lack.

reasons.rubric: Simple boolean current-employment predicate, a clear over-collection by photocopying, but the issuer is each partner employer so the ecosystem is fragmented and frequency is modest.
reasons.validity: Corporate-partner discounts with badge photocopying are real, but a staff-fraud problem is small and employers must run a current-status credential.
reasons.coherence: Parts fit well: current status, revocation, minimal disclosure of the company.
reasons.novelty: Close to idea b11-0 in predicate and issuer, though the verifier and moment differ; employment is not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The copyable-identifier borrowing is only a loose echo and the age-scan borrowing is decorative; the idea reads the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: A store has no known duty to keep the copy, though I cannot confirm.
reasons.linkability: Disclosing the company name plus a revocation check could link purchases to the employer, a modest concern.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Partner employers gain little from running issuance and revocation for discount counters.
reasons.no_wallet: Clerks can continue accepting badges, so a store has little reason to change counter routine.

reasons.rubric: Time-windowed boolean fit-to-travel from a hospital issuer, but the carrier often needs clinical fields, and frequency is low.
reasons.validity: Fit-to-fly notes are real for pregnancy and recent surgery, but airlines' medical desks usually require specific clinical content, and the idea concedes it only covers simpler cases.
reasons.coherence: The sealed-bid analogy does not match the mechanism, which is simply a boolean with an expiry, but the core predicate and issuer fit together.
reasons.novelty: Health-clearance for travel is a moment nobody on the known list touches.
reasons.provenance: The sealed-bid borrowing is decorative, and the minimum-necessary release is a generic principle the idea would state without it.
reasons.retention_law: Airlines may need to keep medical clearance records for liability or aviation rules, and I cannot confirm.
reasons.linkability: A signed short-window attestation from a named hospital can reveal where the holder was treated, a modest leak.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals are cautious about liability for fitness statements and would need to adopt a new issuance flow.
reasons.no_wallet: Passengers can present the paper note, and carriers' MEDIF forms remain the fallback.
